items.d: Passport, citizenship, and notary services for walk-in clients.

One of the most popular summer destinations in South Korea. Haeundae beach attracts tourists from all around the country and gets really overcrowded in late July and early August. Deck chairs and parasols are available to rent for ₩10,000.

This is the largest aquarium in Korea with great facilities and excellent displays. There is also a 3D ride that is worth checking out. There are larger aquariums in Asia, and outside the facility looks rather underwhelming, but inside the

Dongbaekseom is not a real island, but a forested area with Camellia and pine trees past the Westin hotel. It offers a pleasant and short coastal walk, and the APEC Conference Center (with great views of the Gwangali area in Busan) can be v

This is regarded as Busan's 'romantic road', and climbs a hill overlooking the sea. It is often called the Montmartre of Busan by locals, although the two locations only share the attributes of being romantic and on a hill. The majority of
This is a nice forested walk along the sea coast on Dalmaji Hill with an impressive lookout in the middle. At night time the path is lit up.

Contains three art galleries of modern art (one being for children). You can probably feel pretty good about spending 2-3 hours here and feel like you've seen it all. Closed every Monday and January 1st. In case Monday is a national holiday

The Busan International Film Festival has had this impressive open cinema built for the October 2011 festival. Go at night time to appreciate the light show displayed on the ceiling. To get there take the subway/bus to Centum City. The buil

Further along the coast, Songjeong is a 1.2km-long stretch of golden sand in a sheltered cove. There are many hotels and restaurants directly on the beach or within an easy walk. Since it is less crowded, this beach is a better option than

This remarkable Buddhist temple complex is situated on top of a large rock along the ocean. Since most Korean temples are in the mountains this is an unusual location with sweeping ocean views. You need to walk through a market from the car
Buddhist temple and monastery located up Jangsan mountain. Good scenic views over Haeundae.

Although not particularly remarkable compared to Heaundae and Songjeong beaches on eigher side, this village is remote and away from the crowds with some cafes and restaurants by the sea. You can walk here either along the Moontan Road (hil
Museum of Korean traditional art.
Art gallery with exhibitions of works by Korean and international artists. Lovely views over the Korea Strait.

Part of the Shinsigae mall, this spa is probably the most friendly/accessible spa for foreigners in Busan. It is directly on the Centum City subway station, making it very easy to get to. Signs and an Instruction leaflet are also provided i

This boat trip starts off at Haeundae’s Mipo Ferry Terminal and heads towards Oryuk-do Islets and the Igidae area. The shores of Igidae are composed of breathtaking views of fantastically shaped cliffs. This 1-hour boat trip offers great vi

BEXCO is a large exhibition center with many halls, and although most of the events are rather dry (i.e. Industrial Marine technology) there may be something of interest whilst you're in town such as computer gaming or coffee making exposit

If you are near Haeundae, then Jangsan mountain can provide a good day's hiking. There are military bases at the summit complete with minefields (Clearly marked and fenced off), and great views over Busan and on a clear day to Japan. A hike
An old mainline trainline has been repurposed into two types of tourist train - a 'sky capsule' (an elevated small tram) as well a coastal train.

A yachting club with a variety of boats for the public to try out, including tours with a yacht (₩60,000+), a dash around the harbor on a jet boat (₩40,000), Glass bottom boat (₩60,000) and jet skis (₩250,000+)
Korean sauna with separate levels for men and women. Very nice water and views over Haeundae beach. Somewhat out of the way, but if you are visiting Dalmaji road anyway then worth visiting.
Provides trips around Gwangan Bridge and beach in the neighboring area.
A pedestrian street full of fresh food to buy and small restaurants to try out.

A department store with an interesting (albeit expensive) food hall in the basement. It has two cinemas, an ice rink and a large public spa. It is also the biggest department store in the world according to the Guinness World Book of Record

A smaller department store right next to the Shinsegae Department Store. Has a decent cinema as well as a small animal zoo (free) on the top floor. The Kyobo book store is very large and has a large variety of Korean and English books.

items.n: Kim Hee-dae Halmae Wonjo Gamasot Gukbap (Granny Kim Hee-dae'
items.d: Gukbap is a hot bowl of rice and broth, and available in many of the old style restaurants in Heaundae market.
Delicious burgers in hand-made bao buns.
A great option if you're craving vegetables. 5 salad choices and a fruit salad for dessert.

Lee Jae-mo Pizza is known as one of Busan’s representative pizza restaurants, so tourists visiting Busan are encouraged to stop by and try the Lee Jae-mo crust pizza. It’s cheaper than other places, and the cheese flavor is excellent, so I

items.n: Subyeon Choe-go Pork Soup, Millak Main Branch
items.d: There are several chain branches of Subyeon Choegoe Pork Soup, but this is the main branch, so you should go there to enjoy it at its best. The most famous dish is the pork jowl soup with rice, so please be sure to try it.
Hot broths with either chicken or beef cooked with rice and the special Korean ingredient of Ginseng.
Solid Indian fare in a stylish environment.
Really good fish and chips with fresh batter that you can eat outside by the sea. Very long queues on weekends. Also good coffee and ice cream.
Mexican restaurant with a good reputation. Slightly out of the way, but has vegetarian options as well.

items.n: Busan Etteun Godeungeo – Haeundae Main Branch
items.d: A Korean restaurant specializing in wood-fired grilled fish, including grilled mackerel and seasoned grilled mackerel. The fish is cooked in a wood-fired oven heated to over 500°C, and the restaurant also offers a self-service bar with a va
Novotel Ambassador, Haeundae. Steak, fresh seafood, premier wine. Sephia style interior design, cozy atmosphere, and ocean view.
Decent Italian restaurant at the top of Dalmaji Hill with views over the ocean.
Good if you want some familiar western food.
Nice bakery with good snacks for the beach.
In the basement of a hotel, this is an expensive Korean style booking club.
Pool table and cool Americans aplenty on the weekends. Pretty sleepy during most weeknights.
A chain of bars in Busan and a popular place for Koreans and Westerners to intermingle.

Has live DJs and occasional live bands on weekends. Plays requests during the weekdays. Darts, pool and Hookahs available. Though not busy on most weeknights, there are usually a good mix of foreigners and Koreans inside.
A proper pub serving a large variety of premium draft beers and western food. Great place for a mid week dinner and pint or to party on the weekends. Good mix of Koreans and westerners.

Haeundae With Guesthouse is a 5-min walk from Haeundae beach, the common area has a bright open space where you can meet other travellers and locals willing to practice their English. The breakfast is good, you can cook your eggs the style

15-min walk from Haeundae beach, sauna entry alone costs ₩8,000. This is a jjimjilbang and sleeping is on a large communal floor with only a limited supply of mats and pillows. It is locally famed and can get crowded on weekends. The entran
One min to the Haeundae beach, 5 min walk to the Haeundae station. Beautiful natural scenery. Women only.
Owned by Indy, who is a nice guy and very helpful. Well equipped with small pool table, free internet, free movies and free laundry.
Business class hotel as the name suggests. Rooms could be bigger but in room mod cons pretty nice. Some English spoken.
Set back behind the Paradise Hotel, but only a couple of minutes walk to the sea front.

Located in a busy area just a minute's walk from the nearest bus stop, and right in front of Haeundae station, this hotel offers a cozy and relaxing atmosphere, a 20-minute walking from Haeundae Beach and SEA LIFE Busan Aquarium.
New boutique hotel with on-site restaurant, gym, rooftop pool. All rooms have views of Songjeong beach, which is a 10 minute walk away. 15 minute walk from Songjeong railway station.
An upscale hotel on the boardwalk of Haeundae beach. Has excellent hot spring facilities with a view directly over the beach. (used to be the Novotel).

This hotel has an extensive range of facilities including duty-free shops in the basement, one (rather small) outdoor pool, a full service spa, gym, outdoor hot spring (with a view of the ocean), sauna, as well as a casino inside the hotel
A luxury hotel at the west end of Haeundae beach and next to Dongbaek Island. It's set back a bit further away (about 1 km) from the downtown Haeundae area.

Unlike the three hotels above which are on the boardwalk or on the beach, this one is off the boardwalk, however still very close to the beach (about five minutes walk). Good amenities but each (swimming pool, gym, etc.) charges separately.

A luxury hotel in the Haeundae marine city, overlooking the ocean and Gwangan Bridge. This hotel offers a variety of dining and entertainment options, a fitness center, seven spa treatment rooms, an indoor pool, and 269 guestrooms including

Best experienced at night when the impressive Gwangan Grand Bridge is illuminated. The area is similar to Haeundae but smaller and less upscale. There are plenty of local restaurants, bars and shops in the area. In summer the crowds are sli

Driving (or taking the bus) across Gwangan Bridge is a great way to see the view, especially at nighttime. Viewed from the town it has an impressive light display at night. It featured in the Marvel movie 'Black Panther'.
Here is a park where people can see Gwangan grand bridge and Gwangalli beach.

This mountain offers one of the best panoramic views of Busan, including Gwangalli Beach, the Gwangan Grand Bridge, and the cityscape. The view is especially breathtaking at night. The peak features an observation deck and a beacon fire sta

A unique cultural complex built in a former wire factory. It features a popular bookstore (Yes24), a local brewery (Praha Pub), a Starbucks, and various exhibition spaces. A great place to relax and enjoy the modern, artistic atmosphere.
A community hub that hosts various performances, exhibitions, and cultural classes. It's a great place to experience local arts and culture.
A famous street lined with cherry blossom trees, creating a beautiful pink canopy in the spring. It's one of Busan's most popular spots for enjoying the cherry blossom season.
A unique restaurant known for its seafood dishes and lively atmosphere. It offers a great view of the beach and bridge, making it a popular spot for both locals and tourists.
Suyeong History Park preserves the remains of the former Suyeong-eupseong fortress from the Joseon Dynasty. Informational signs explain the historical significance of the site.
A local market offering fresh produce, street food, and daily necessities. It provides insight into everyday life in Suyeong and is popular with residents.
A well-known Catholic church in the Namcheon area, recognized for its architecture and role as a local religious center.
A paved cycling and walking route along the Suyeong River, frequently used by locals for exercise and commuting.
A temporary night market operating during peak tourist seasons, featuring street food, snacks, and small craft vendors along the beachfront.
A small urban regeneration project featuring murals and street art painted on residential walls, offering casual photo opportunities and quiet walks.
An open beachfront space used for public performances, cultural events, and seasonal festivals. Visitors may encounter street performances or small-scale concerts depending on the event schedule.
A neighborhood public space used for small exhibitions, community events, and outdoor gatherings. Primarily serves residents but is accessible to visitors.
A public cultural venue hosting exhibitions, performances, and local cultural events that are open to residents and visitors.
Archaeological remains marking the original gate location of Suyeong-eupseong, with signage explaining its historical role during the Joseon period.
A designated area offering seasonal marine leisure activities such as kayaking and paddleboarding, popular with visitors during summer months.
A small cluster of ceramic studios and craft shops known among visitors interested in local arts and handmade goods.

A raw fish festival held annually in October. The event, which takes place on the sandy expanse of Gwangalli Beach, is a lively celebration of Busan's seafood culture. Visitors can participate in a variety of activities, including making ho

The Busan Fireworks Festival takes place every October along Gwangalli Beach, transforming the city's iconic shoreline into a dazzling spectacle of light and sound. Drawing millions of spectators each year, it stands as one of South Korea's

Each year, the Gwangan Bridge is opened to the public for a walking festival. This unique event allows you to walk or run across Busan’s most famous landmark, an opportunity not available at any other time of the year. The walk offers spect
A traditional fishing culture festival recreating Joseon-era coastal life with performances, seafood events, and hands-on cultural programs for visitors.
Seasonal outdoor yoga sessions organized along Gwangalli Beach, open to visitors looking for wellness-focused seaside activities.
Temporary street markets featuring local food, crafts, and small performances, occasionally organized during seasonal events.
A designated beachfront zone where digital lighting and media installations are periodically displayed, creating a modern night-time atmosphere for visitors.

Gwangalli Beach is a hub for water sports, with stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) being the most popular activity. You can easily rent equipment and get lessons from one of the many rental shops along the beach. Paddle out onto the calm waters

Take a leisurely cruise along the Suyeonggang River, which flows through the heart of the district. The tour offers a different perspective of Suyeong's scenic beauty, passing by the APEC Naru Park and under a series of beautiful bridges. I

As the sun sets, Gwangalli Beach transforms into an outdoor stage for talented buskers. You can find musicians, dancers, and artists performing along the boardwalk, creating a lively and energetic atmosphere. The busking culture is a major

A must-see attraction on Gwangalli Beach is the spectacular M-Drone Show. Every Saturday, hundreds of synchronized drones light up the night sky, creating intricate shapes and animations above the Gwangan Bridge. The show features a differe

For a more active and scenic experience, rent a bike and cycle along the well-maintained paths of the Suyeonggang River. The path offers a peaceful escape from the crowded beach area, with beautiful views of the river, lush greenery, and th

The streets facing Gwangalli Beach are lined with a diverse selection of cafes, each offering a unique atmosphere and, most importantly, a prime view of the ocean and bridge. From trendy, minimalist cafes to cozy, themed spots, there's a pl

Walk down the charming streets behind Gwangalli Beach, and you'll discover a collection of unique, independently owned prop shops. These stores are a treasure trove for anyone looking for special, handcrafted souvenirs, whimsical stationery

A modern, multi-story cultural complex on the water with a stunning view of the Gwangan Bridge. It is a popular hangout spot with small shops, art galleries, and pop-up stores. The ground floor offers a selection of trendy fashion items, un

For an authentic and truly local experience. On the first floor, you can select fresh seafood directly from the vendors, who are eager to show off their catch of the day. Once you've made your choice, you can take your purchase upstairs to

A traditional market that offers a glimpse into local life. While not as large as other famous markets, it's a great place to find fresh produce, local street food, and everyday goods at affordable prices.

items.d: A large supermarket where you can find everything from groceries to electronics and household items.

This traditional market is less touristy than others and provides a vibrant glimpse into daily life in Busan. You can find everything from fresh produce and seafood to delicious street food and household goods. It's a great spot to grab a c
A popular health and beauty store for Korean cosmetics and daily necessities.
A large discount store selling household items and travel essentials.
A footwear and sportswear store offering international brands.

A beloved seafood restaurant and izakaya-style eatery specializing in clams, shellfish, and grilled seafood. It’s a local favorite for late-night dining with cold drinks and lively social atmosphere close to Gwangalli Beach.

A highly rated Korean barbecue restaurant in the Gwangalli area, known for generous portions of grilled meats and quality side dishes. The lively atmosphere and beachside location make it an excellent dinner choice after sightseeing or beac
A highly rated casual restaurant focused on salmon and seafood bowls, sushi, and creative fish dishes. Often recommended for seafood lovers looking for a more modern menu near the beach.
A long-established local restaurant serving pork soup, a Busan specialty, often recommended to visitors seeking affordable and authentic regional food.

Busan is famous for raw fish ('회 Hway'), which the Koreans eat in the same style as bulgogi, namely topped with kimchi and gochujang and wrapped in a lettuce leaf. One of the best places to sample this is in a large brown building at the no

The owner, Mr. Jun, speaks English, and ordering here is easy: it's either set A, B or C. Even Set A is huge, while C is extremely large. This is as real as it gets and dishes will include still-moving octopus tentacles and other stuff most
A local favorite for fresh sashimi and traditional Korean seafood stews. Known for its high quality and authentic flavors, often featuring seasonal catches.
A classic Busan-style pork and rice soup. This restaurant is in the Suyeong Gukbap alley and is known for its deep, flavorful broth.
A famous Busan chain specializing in 'Nak-Gop-Sae' (spicy octopus, beef intestine, and shrimp casserole). A hearty and spicy meal, perfect for sharing.
A branch of one of Busan's most famous 'milmyeon' (wheat noodle) restaurants. Offers refreshing cold noodles, both spicy (bibim) and non-spicy (mul).
A humble restaurant near Millak Port serving delicious handmade noodle soup (kalguksu) and pajeon (green onion pancake).
A long-standing local favorite for charcoal-grilled pork ribs (dwaeji galbi). The atmosphere is lively and often packed with locals.
An upscale Italian restaurant with a direct view of the Gwangan Bridge. Specializes in pasta, risotto, and steak.
A popular expatriate-run bar with a friendly atmosphere. Serves excellent Western pub food, including burgers, wings, and fish and chips. Great selection of craft beers.
A popular gourmet burger joint. Known for its juicy, handcrafted patties and fresh ingredients. Often has a line.
A casual New York-style pizzeria selling large slices. A perfect late-night snack to grab and eat by the beach.
A lively Spanish tapas bar serving authentic dishes like gambas al ajillo and paella. Great atmosphere with sangria and wine, plus a good view.
A casual pizza and pub-style restaurant serving pizzas, craft beers, and light dishes. With its beachfront proximity, it’s a popular evening gathering spot for travelers and locals.
A cozy, authentic Japanese izakaya specializing in yakitori (grilled skewers) and various small dishes. Pairs well with sake or beer.
Authentic Thai food restaurant run by a Thai chef. Popular for its Pad Thai and Tom Yum Goong.
A simple, no-frills Vietnamese restaurant serving excellent pho (beef noodle soup) and banh mi. Quick, delicious, and affordable.
Australian-style cafe with variations on brunch and lunch classics.
A very popular cafe on the main beach road, famous for its multi-story glass windows offering unobstructed views of the bridge. Great for coffee and elaborate desserts.
A "newtro" (new-retro) style cafe known for its quiet atmosphere and specialty hand-drip coffee.
A bakery known for its savory breads (like onion or corn bread) and freshly baked goods. A local favorite for breakfast.
A well-known specialty coffee café directly facing Gwangalli Beach, popular with tourists for high-quality coffee and clear views of Gwangan Bridge both during the day and at night.
A premium café brand offering espresso-based drinks in a comfortable setting, often used by tourists as a rest stop while walking along the beachfront.
A popular dessert café known for its donuts and colorful interior, frequently visited by tourists and younger visitors walking along Gwangalli Beach.
‘The Brewery’ is Busan’s first American-style craft beer microbrewery and brewpub.
A popular choice on Gwangalli Beach, offering stunning views of the Gwangan Bridge. The hotel has a sophisticated, modern feel and is known for its spacious rooms.

This hotel offers a modern and clean stay with a fantastic beachfront location. Many rooms feature panoramic views of the ocean and the Gwangan Bridge. The rooftop bar is a major highlight, providing one of the best night views in the area.

Known for its large-scale water park and spa facilities, this hotel is a top choice for families. The rooms are comfortable, and the hotel's main draw is the indoor and outdoor water activities it offers.

A budget-friendly hotel slightly further down the beach from the main strip. While it's not on the main beachfront, it offers great views of the Gwangan Bridge from higher floors. It’s a solid option for budget-conscious travelers.
This stylish hotel has a chic and modern interior design. It has a vibrant atmosphere. Many of the rooms offer fantastic views of the water and the bridge.

A classic motel option offering simple, clean rooms at a very affordable price. It's a good choice for travelers on a tight budget who prioritize location over amenities. You'll find yourself right across from the beach with easy access to

A sleek, modern hotel with stylish rooms and incredible views of the Gwangan Bridge. Its minimalist design and comfortable bedding make it a popular choice for a relaxing stay. The hotel is within walking distance of the beach and several d

A popular choice for its unique, artistically designed rooms. Located on the beach, many of its rooms offer a perfect view of the Gwangan Bridge. It is especially famous for its "photo zone" rooms and a cozy café on the ground floor. Perfec

A modern hotel with an excellent location near the beach. It offers well-maintained rooms, many of which have balconies with beautiful ocean views. The hotel is a great value for the price, providing a comfortable and relaxing stay away fro
A charming and cozy hotel. The rooms are clean, bright, and simply decorated. It’s on a quieter street just a short walk from the beach.

A more business-oriented hotel slightly inland from the beach, closer to the Namcheon station area. The rooms are clean, spacious, and well-equipped with modern amenities. It offers easy access to the subway system.

A few streets of a grubby district have been 'restored' to their condition in the post-Korean War 1960s, with wooden lamppost and bronze figures illustrating scenes of hardscrabble street life. Also easy walking distance to Yongdusan Park.

This is possibly Korea's most famous fish market with a large selection of seafood there. You will have to opportunity to eat squid that is still wriggling when you eat it! Try to come very early to see the activity around the fish being la

As a symbolic location for the Busan International Film Festival, BIFF Square features handprints of famous film directors and actors. Once a district with a high concentration of theaters, it is now a representative street food destination

Songdo beach was apparently the first official beach in Korea and the main attraction in Busan for many years until Haeundae became the main tourist center. Today the beach is small (450 meters) and quiet with some charm, surrounded by low

Gamcheon village was a Korean war refugee camp, and backwater outside of the city center. In 2008 it attracted the attention of local university students who began painting murals throughout the village as part of their social service activ

items.n: Busan Air Cruise (Songdo Marine Cable Car)

Home of Busan's Chinese community with cheap and delicious dumplings, though most of the Chinese have left the area, and it is today mainly home to Russians.
This is an example of old, steep residential area of Busan that was formed after Korean War. Although you can walk the famous 168 steps, there is a free monorail that takes you uphill.

Named after King Taejong Muyul (654-661) of the Silla Dynasty who practiced archery here after unifying the Three Kingdoms. During the Joseon period, King Taejong (1400-1418) is reputed to have visited here for recreation and pleasure. The

This was a US military base that was turned into a large park in 2014. The parks have large playground for kids and remnants of military base. The park museum has many artifacts about the history of the US military base and the lives around
Discover the history of Busan from the Prehistoric period to the present day.

This is the only United Nations cemetery in the world. Soldiers from many countries who contributed to the United Nations during the Korean War are buried here. Take bus from in front of the Memorial Park after subway exit. Please note that

If you are interested in the industrial side of Busan then the Port tour is hard to beat. Passengers on board can see the port facilities of Busan Port, including the passenger terminal, general piers, and container terminals. You will lear
All-day ticket available for double decker tour buses.

In 2014 a new zoo opened in Busan, with a variety of animals (tigers, lions, bears, elephants, monkeys, etc.) It is very much targeted at children, and there is a very good activity center at the end, with climbing ropes and other activitie

An old, easily overlooked market near Jagalchi Market in Nampo dong. There is nothing this market doesn’t sell. Since Busan has a big harbor, many foreigners have visited, so that it was quite early when citizens of Busan began to accept ex

items.n: The markets of Gukje, Gwangbok-dong and Nampo-dong
items.d: Three major shopping districts connected to each other. Very much similar to Seoul's Namdaemun Market and Myeongdong shopping district. Various shops geared towards young and old people with many brand name stores and underground stores. Yo

items.n: Lotte Department Store, Busan Main Branch
items.d: An over-the-top temple to consumerism (check out the fountains and statues at the basement entrance), this is Busan's second largest department store. It is the place to pick up some ₩500,000 ginseng or perhaps a Spam gift set for the folks

This is a similar Lotte department store, and has an indoor vertical waterfall and rooftop observation deck which has a whole view of the harbor and bridges. With a sales area of 23,097 pyeong, it is the largest store in Busan and the third

Serves up gimbap from ₩2000 and all sorts of noodles for ₩2500-4000. No English menu or sign, but if you can say it they'll make it, and it's open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
This food court serves all the usual Korean favorites, with plastic food and English menus making ordering a snap.
Specializes in beef soups and kakkduggi side dish.

European, North American, Russian, and SE Asian dishes; try the borscht stew. Popular with sailors and their lady companions, the best time to go is after midnight. A small shop offering a limited selection of dust-covered western goods is

Turns into a bar, but they serve excellent Western food, and American-style breakfast until the afternoon. Open air bar. Thursday is ladies' bottomless drinks for ₩15000. In-Jung runs the bar and is a great hostess.
Tteokbokki restaurant is inside the can market. Prices are reasonable at ₩5,000 for tteokbokki, ₩5,000 for fries, and ₩1,000 for a corn dog.
Authentic Indian restaurant owned by Indians.

This is the most famous pizza restaurant in Central Busan. On weekdays and weekends, a very large number of people line up to eat inside the restaurant. To solve this problem, a take-out only store has been opened across the street. Prices

This is a pork cutlet version of the Korean fried chicken called 'Pork Ribs Fried'. It is available in large, medium, and small sizes, with prices ranging from ₩13,000 to ₩23,000 depending on the size.

This Chinese restaurant in Busan, Jung-gu, is famous for its yuni-jjajang and sweet and sour pork. Noodles and fried rice are inexpensive at ₩6,000-8,000, but other dishes cost ₩20,000-30,000. Closed every Wednesday.
It's a Chinese restaurant. Typically, there are regular course meals (₩37,000-85,000 ), lunch course meals (₩23,000-35,000), and couple course meals (₩39,000-49,000), with a 15:30 - 16:30 break.

A Korean barbecue restaurant with a single menu item: beef outside skirt It costs ₩13,000 per bowl and has sides such as Doenjangjjigae, rice, and Naengmyeon. Closed every Sunday and last order is at 21:00.

Friendly atmosphere, staff speak excellent English and know their way around town. There are many restaurants, shops, and bars near the guesthouse. No curfew. They have 6-, 4-person dormitory room and twin, double bed room.
Offers Korean lessons for their guests. They have dinner with their guests. The hostel near the Kyungsung-Pukyong University area also features a gorgeous ocean view.

Close to Yongdusan Park, this Busan tourist hotel is a 4-minute walk from Exit 7 of Nampo Station on Busan Line 1. International Market, Jagalchi Market, and BIFF Square are a 15-minute walk away, while Gwangalli Beach is a 40-minute drive

Attached to one of the largest shopping centers in Busan. All of the staff speak very good English, and the rooms are quite large with great views of the city surrounding it. The hotel also offers a casino on the second floor, an Irish pub,
From Busan Station, take Subway Line 1 for one stop and get off at Jungang Station, then walk 200 meters to Exit 14, opposite Jungang Police Station. It costs ₩130,000-150,000 per night.

Next to Yongdusan Park, Tower Hill Hotel has a fitness center, massage parlour and restaurants. There is also free parking available. There are 116 rooms, all with free Wi-Fi. In-room amenities include a refrigerator, a coffee pot, and a sa

The hotel is about a 5-minute walk from Exit 12 of Nampo Station on Busan Subway Line 1. Jagalchi Market is just a 3-minute walk away, Gukje Market is about a 10-minute walk away, and Songdo Beach is a 15-minute drive away. It's also a 25-m
The area around the PNU is very lively. It is full of students, bars, cafes and fashion shops. You can try Korean student food specialties. Note that it retains the old spelling of 'Pusan'.

An open historical plaza built around the remains of Dongnae Eupseong, allowing visitors to explore restored fortress walls, information panels, and surrounding heritage sites that explain Busan’s defensive history during the Joseon period.
An archaeological site featuring ancient burial mounds from the Gaya and early Silla periods, offering visitors a rare opportunity to see excavated tomb structures within an urban residential area.

A Confucian academy from the Joseon Dynasty, historically used for education and ceremonial rites. Visitors can explore traditional architecture and gain insight into Korea’s classical education system in a quiet setting.

Busan’s main professional baseball stadium and home of the Lotte Giants, Sajik Baseball Stadium is known nationwide for its energetic atmosphere and passionate local fans. Even for visitors unfamiliar with Korean baseball, attending a game
Famous for its stunning panoramic night views, this pass is a favorite spot for late-night drives and photography.
A historical memorial street dedicated to the 1919 independence movement at Gupo Market, featuring murals and monuments.

One of Korea's great temples, this large complex is located up in the mountains and feels further away from the city than the few kilometers that it really is. The buildings have been destroyed and rebuilt many times since they were founded
A quieter temple nestled in the foothills of Geumjeongsan, offering a peaceful cultural stop with traditional Buddhist architecture and surroundings emphasizing spiritual calm.
Take bus number 29, 29-1, 89 or 129 and walk for five minutes.

Another impressive temple is about 90 minutes' hike from the cable car station. It is often overlooked, but has magnificent statues carved into the mountain itself. Great views over Busan and very peaceful. From the South Gate (남문), the pat
A distinctive Islamic place of worship and cultural site serving Busan’s Muslim community. Visitors can admire the Middle Eastern architectural style and explore cultural diversity in northern Busan.
South Korea's largest collection of sealife exhibits, with giant squid, whale sharks and oarfish.
A museum dedicated to traditional folk customs, crafts, and rituals of Busan and surrounding regions, helping visitors understand everyday life and seasonal traditions of Korea.
Roman Catholic museum dedicated to eight Christian martyrs who were killed for their faith in 1868.
A local history museum documenting the development of Geumjeong District, featuring archival materials, photographs, and exhibitions focused on urban and cultural change.
A university museum displaying archaeological artifacts, folk items, and regional history exhibits related to southeastern Korea.
An educational facility introducing the Nakdong River ecosystem. Visitors can participate in interactive exhibits focused on environmental conservation.
A small exhibition area highlighting Busan’s baseball culture and the history of Sajik Stadium. It offers insight into one of the city’s most passionate local sports traditions.
A small gallery preserving photographs and documents related to Geumjeong-gu’s urban development. Visitors can gain insight into how the district evolved alongside the university area.
Offers commanding views over the city of Busan. It can be reached via a relatively steep 2-km climb of the mountain behind the Beomeosa Temple.
An ecological exhibition center introducing migratory birds and wetland ecosystems of the Nakdong River estuary, popular among visitors interested in nature conservation and environmental education.
A botanical garden featuring diverse flora native to Korea and abroad, located on the slopes of Geumjeongsan. Excellent for nature lovers and families exploring outdoor attractions.
A public arboretum featuring native Korean trees and plants, offering educational displays and seasonal scenery that attract visitors interested in nature and environmental learning.
An open grass area along the Nakdong River suitable for casual picnics and relaxation. Visitors can observe local leisure culture in a spacious riverside environment.
A public cultural venue hosting exhibitions, performances, and regional history programs, offering visitors insight into Dongnae’s traditional arts and contemporary cultural activities.
A public venue hosting performances, exhibitions, and cultural classes. Visitors can attend concerts or art events reflecting local culture.

An educational center introducing the natural environment and forest culture of Geumjeongsan. Exhibits and programs focus on conservation and local ecology, making it a useful stop for visitors before or after exploring nearby hiking trails

A small cultural street connecting historic sites, galleries, and local workshops in Dongnae. Visitors can explore murals, exhibitions, and traditional architecture while gaining a sense of the district’s historical identity and everyday cu
A public classroom space hosting cultural and creative workshops. Travelers may participate in short programs or observe local community activities.

items.p: Entry to the spa is ₩8000, plus ₩2,000 for the jjimjilbang
items.h: The spa is closed in May for vacation and re-opens in June.
items.d: This massive hot spring complex claims to be the largest in Asia: Noboribetsu might disagree, but it certainly is huge, with hot, tepid, cold and strawberry milk-filled baths, saunas, pools, and an outdoor section. On the 3rd floor is a lar

Nice park at the foot of the mountains in North Busan. There are some small amusement rides for children as well. The highlight is the cable car that takes you to the top of the mountain near Namsam Gate. (Note that some signs call the cabl
A public foot bath supplied with natural hot spring water from Dongnae Oncheon, allowing visitors to relax and experience the area’s traditional spa culture without entering a full bathhouse.
A cultural experience allowing visitors to observe or participate in traditional Korean archery, offering insight into historic martial practices associated with Confucian values.
A public ice rink used for skating and events, often visited by families and tourists during winter months as part of Buk-gu’s recreational facilities.
A guided tour program explaining archaeological findings from the Bokcheon-dong tombs, allowing visitors to gain deeper understanding of ancient burial customs and artifacts.
An educational activity offering guided learning sessions about wetlands, migratory birds, and river ecosystems, designed for visitors interested in environmental conservation.
Short-term cultural and craft workshops open to the public, allowing visitors to participate in hands-on learning experiences related to Korean daily culture.
Interactive science programs designed for visitors of all ages, featuring hands-on experiments and demonstrations that make science accessible and engaging.

A multi-purpose sports facility near Hwamyeong Ecological Park offering open-access outdoor fields and courts for soccer, baseball, tennis, basketball, and other community sports. With scenic surroundings near the Nakdong River, the complex

A community-based urban farming site where visitors can learn about small-scale agriculture and sustainability practices. Occasionally hosting workshops and hands-on programs, it offers travelers a chance to observe local efforts toward eco
An outdoor fitness park equipped with exercise machines used by local residents. Visitors can casually join in physical activity while observing everyday recreational culture in Dongnae.
A practice space for traditional Korean music groups. Visitors may observe rehearsals or attend small public sessions, offering exposure to regional performing arts.
An impressive temple about 90 minutes hike from the cable car station. It is often overlooked, but has magnificent statues carved into the mountain itself. Great views over Busan and very peaceful.

The main ridge trail of Geumjeongsan offers panoramic views over Busan and access to fortress remains. It is a popular by hikers and visitors seeking Busan’s mountain landscape frequently choose this route.
A historic hiking route following the walls of Geumjeongsanseong Fortress. Hikers can enjoy forest paths combined with cultural heritage, making it popular among history-oriented visitors.
A neighborhood mountain trail offering moderate hiking conditions and views over Dongnae district. Popular with locals for short but rewarding hikes.
A forested mountain path inside Geumgang Park, suitable for light hiking combined with nature observation and city views.
A local hiking trail connecting low mountain ridges near Hwamyeong Ecological Park, often chosen by hikers seeking calm river-and-mountain scenery.
A long-distance hiking-friendly riverside trail allowing visitors to experience wetlands, bird habitats, and open landscapes along the Nakdong River.

Hwamyeong Gichatgil is a 1.2-km-long forest trail created along the active Gyeongbu Line railway. What was once a neglected space next to the tracks has been transformed into a beautiful themed path filled with Metasequoia, pine, and variou
A peaceful ecological trail following the Daecheoncheon stream. It is a favorite local spot for birdwatching and enjoying the clear water flowing from Geumjeongsan Mountain.
A trekking path connecting ancient prehistoric dolmens and cultural heritage sites in the Geumgok area.

A large supermarket popular with visitors for purchasing Korean snacks, daily goods, and souvenirs. Conveniently located near Dongnae Station, making it accessible for travelers staying in northern Busan.
A health and beauty store offering popular Korean cosmetics, skincare products, and travel essentials, frequently visited by tourists seeking K-beauty items.
A mid-sized department store featuring fashion, cosmetics, and food courts, serving as a convenient shopping destination for visitors exploring the Buk-gu area.
A traditional local market selling fresh produce, street food, and household goods, offering visitors a glimpse into everyday shopping culture in northern Busan.
A large discount store selling household items, travel accessories, and daily necessities, often used by tourists staying near the Nakdong River area.
A campus bookstore selling books, stationery, and university-branded goods. Visitors often purchase souvenirs related to Busan National University.
A small shop offering traditional crafts and regional souvenirs related to Dongnae history, often visited by tourists after museum visits.
Small electronics and accessory shops clustered near the hot spring district.
A small shop selling temple-related souvenirs and traditional goods.
A small shop selling handmade goods produced by local artisans.
A long-running local restaurant specializing in sundae gukbap. Popular among both residents and visitors for its rich broth and generous portions.
A well-known local restaurant specializing in Busan-style pork soup, frequently recommended to visitors seeking an authentic and affordable regional dish.
A traditional Korean restaurant serving loach soup, popular among visitors interested in experiencing regional comfort food near the Nakdong River.
A famous restaurant serving Dongnae-style green onion pancakes, a regional specialty often introduced to tourists as a traditional local dish.
A popular Japanese-style pork cutlet restaurant near Pusan National University. The menu includes loin, tenderloin, Berkshire K pork cutlets, and katsudon.
Thursday Party is a popular pub chain in Korea, and the Pusan National University branch is famous among students for its casual atmosphere, cocktails, and affordable beer.
Close to the Hurshimchung Spa and has a German brewery.
You can stay at the Beomeosa temple, learning and practicing Buddhism. This is immersive, so it should not really treated like a hotel.
The mountain road behind Mandeok is famous for a wide selection of love motels
A modern and stylish hotel situated in the busy Myeongnyun/Dongnae area. It offers clean facilities and easy access to shopping malls and restaurants nearby.
A historic hotel in the Oncheonjang area. Guests can enjoy natural hot spring water directly in the hotel. It is close to Geumgang Park and has good accessibility to Mount Geumjeongsan.
A straightforward business hotel close to Pusan National University and the Guseo commercial district. It offers clean rooms at a reasonable price, with many amenities nearby.
Located in the heart of the Pusan National University area, this hotel is suitable for younger travelers. It's surrounded by countless affordable restaurants, bars, and cafes.
A modern facility offering good value in the Hwamyeong-dong commercial area. It's a convenient spot for exploring the nearby Nakdong River Waterfront Park.
A stylish, boutique-style hotel near a major transportation hub. It is a good choice for travelers using the KTX train line or Busan Metro Line 3 to connect to other parts of the country.
A simple, affordable option in the Gupo area. It's well-suited for budget travelers and those prioritizing proximity to the traditional Gupo Market.
A relatively new and clean hotel offering comfortable stays. It’s located in a quiet area of Hwamyeong, but still close to restaurants and shops.

A convenient and modern hotel located directly beside the subway station, offering excellent connectivity. It’s ideal for business travelers or tourists looking for a comfortable base to explore both Busan and nearby areas.
A stylish but affordable accommodation option that provides a good alternative to love motels in the area. Rooms are generally clean and feature unique, modern decor.

items.n: Nakdong River Estuary Migratory Bird Sanctuary
items.d: The spot where the Nakdong River meets the South Sea has been declared a natural monument since 1966. Where the large mouth of the river forms, there are sand dunes and deltas and many small islands (including Ilung-do). It is now a bird sa

This beach might be the least famous beach in Busan. It is right next to Nakdong river, so it has very soft sand and the water is very shallow. There are small park, fountains, locker room, and small benches for watching the sunset. Among t
Janglim Harbor (inlet) is surrounded by many colorful buildings and boats, a popular spot for strolling or taking pictures.

items.p: Free to enter, but some experiences or workshops may have a fee
items.h: Open all year, but most shops and galleries are open from 09:00 to 18:00
items.d: A village with colorful houses built in a stair-step fashion on the foothills of a coastal mountain. It is known for its narrow alleys, art installations, and panoramic views.
A large park on an island at the mouth of the Nakdong River. It is a major migratory bird habitat and features walking trails, bike paths, and a bird-watching center.
A scenic rocky headland with walking trails and a dense forest. It's a great spot for a hike with views of the sea, Dadaepo Beach, and nearby islands.

items.h: Show times vary by season. Check the official website for schedules.
items.d: A spectacular musical fountain show with lights and water jets. It's a popular attraction, especially in the evening, as it's located right on Dadaepo Beach.
An observatory offering a panoramic view of the Nakdong River Estuary, the sand dunes, and Dadaepo Beach. It's an excellent spot for photographers.
One of Busan's largest traditional markets, selling everything from clothes and household goods to street food. It's a bustling place with a rich history.
A historic alley filled with secondhand bookstores, some of which have been around for generations. It’s a nostalgic and peaceful place for book lovers.
Korea's largest seafood market. You can see vendors selling fresh fish and seafood, and many restaurants on the upper floors will cook your selections on the spot.
A city park with the iconic Busan Tower at its center. It offers great views of the city and the harbor and features statues, flower beds, and a museum.
A village built along a cliff overlooking the sea. It's known for its scenic coastal path, art galleries, and cafes. It was also a filming location for a famous Korean movie.
Offers milmyeon (wheat noodles), a regional food item. Both cold noodles (mul milmyeon) and spicy mixed noodles (bibim milmyeon) are available.
Sells tteok-bokki (spicy rice cakes) and eomuk (fish cakes). Provides a typical local street food experience.
Serves seafood rice dishes and grilled fish options. The location provides views of the ocean and the Songdo Marine Cable Car.
Specializes in nakji bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus) and nakgop-sae (octopus, tripe, and shrimp casserole). The dishes are noted for their high spice level.
A cluster of restaurants serving jokbal, a dish of marinated and boiled pig's feet. Various preparations, including cold sliced versions, are available.
Several small vendors and cafes offering quick meals and snacks such as ramyeon (instant noodles), kimbap (seaweed rice rolls), and beverages for sightseers.
Offers hoe (raw fish/sashimi) and seafood sets. The location provides a view of the ocean.
Serves dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), a staple Busan dish. Noted for its rich, clear pork broth.
An all-you-can-eat establishment focusing on grilled clams and shellfish (jogae gui).
Serves handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup). The broth is traditionally anchovy-based.

This establishment specializes in various Korean pancakes, notably the thick, savory nokdu jeon (mung bean pancake) and haemul pajeon (seafood green onion pancake). The dishes are made from freshly prepared ingredients.

A local eatery that serves milmyeon (wheat noodles), a food item associated with Busan. The restaurant offers both the chilled broth version (mul milmyeon) and the spicy mixed version (bibim milmyeon).
Specializes in jangeo maeuntang (spicy eel stew). The dish is served in a communal pot, combining fresh eel, vegetables, and spicy seasoning. It is a typical local favorite in the coastal region.
Serves tteokgalbi (grilled short rib patties), which are ground, seasoned, and grilled beef or pork. The meal typically includes rice and a set of traditional side dishes (banchan).

A typical seafood restaurant in the area that offers jogae gui (grilled shellfish). Patrons select their seafood, which is then cooked at the table on a charcoal grill. Operating hours are generally geared toward the evening dining market.

This restaurant specializes in seolleongtang (ox bone soup), which is characterized by its white, milky broth from hours of slow cooking. The soup is usually served with rice and minimal seasoning, allowing diners to adjust the flavor thems
The main item served here is budae jjigae (army stew), a dish cooked at the table in a large pot. Ingredients typically include ham, sausage, baked beans, kimchi, and ramen noodles in a spicy broth.
A restaurant that focuses on haemul kalguksu (seafood knife-cut noodles). The noodles are typically hand-cut and served in a broth enriched by clams, mussels, and other seasonal seafood.
Operates on a unique model where guests purchase fresh cuts of Hanwoo (premium Korean beef) directly from the butcher shop section and then cook the meat themselves at tables equipped with grills.
Serves sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup with rice). The soup contains Korean-style blood sausage (sundae) and various pork offal in a dense, rich broth. It is open at all hours.

Specializes in kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), a dish traditionally associated with the Gupo area. The noodles are typically served in a clean, anchovy-based broth. This location is one of the long-standing original stores in the district.

This alley features multiple eateries specializing in dakbal (spicy chicken feet), a popular local late-night dish. Visitors can choose between boneless or bone-in versions, usually accompanied by alcoholic beverages.
Serves haemul tang (spicy seafood stew). The stew is prepared with a variety of fresh seasonal seafood, crabs, and shellfish in a spicy broth, designed to be shared by several people.
A small, themed eatery within the cultural village serving grilled meat skewers and simple rice dishes. It is primarily geared toward tourists looking for a quick and casual meal while sightseeing.

Specializes in sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew). The stew is served boiling hot and can be customized with seafood or meat, accompanied by traditional side dishes. Popular as a simple breakfast or lunch option.
The primary dish is jangeo cheopbap (grilled eel on rice), often prepared in a Japanese style with a sweet glaze. It is considered a specialty meal in the area.
Offers several varieties of traditional Korean stews (jjigae) served in individual earthenware pots (ttukbaegi). Options usually include kimchi jjigae, doenjang jjigae, and sundubu jjigae.

Specializes in bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), which are traditionally pan-fried until crispy. This dish is often paired with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) and is primarily open during evening hours.
Focuses on galbi jjim (braised short ribs), a traditional slow-cooked beef or pork dish. The meat is braised in a soy sauce-based marinade with vegetables and served in a hot pot.

A typical seaside restaurant offering various grilled whole fish (saengseon gui), such as mackerel and hairtail. The dishes are usually served as a set with rice and several small side dishes (banchan).

An area containing several small, traditional pubs (jumoek) specializing in makgeolli (Korean rice wine). Various regional makgeolli types and accompanying traditional side dishes (anju) are served. This spot is popular among locals for a c

This street offers various cafes and pubs with views of the ocean and the Songdo Marine Cable Car. Many places serve light drinks, including craft beer and wine, alongside coffee. Suitable for those seeking a relaxing, scenic evening.
A casual bar offering a selection of beer and mixed drinks. Its location is utilized to provide sunset views over Dadaepo Beach, particularly popular before or after the fountain show.
A cluster of hoega (Korean-style beer bars) that specialize in draft beer and fried chicken (chimaek). This area provides a lively, high-energy environment typical of Korean urban nightlife.
A non-alcoholic cafe that offers coffee, tea, and juice. The main draw is the high vantage point providing panoramic views of the colorful Gamcheon village houses.
Serves traditional Korean teas such as sanga-cha (twin citrus tea) and sujeonggwa (cinnamon punch). This spot provides a quiet setting away from the commercial areas, suitable for daytime relaxation.
A modern pub that features a rotating selection of local and imported craft beers on tap. They also offer simple food items (anju) designed to accompany beer.

An authentic Korean pojangmacha (tent bar) experience specializing in Soju and simple, hearty food. The plastic tent structure and outdoor seating are characteristic of this type of casual drinking spot.
A small bar that offers a curated selection of global wines, sold by the glass or bottle. It provides a quieter, more upscale alternative to the neighboring beer and soju spots.

items.p: Room rates vary / Alcohol packages required
items.d: A series of large, multi-room karaoke complexes (noraebang) that require the purchase of alcohol and food along with the room rental fee. This venue type is intended for group entertainment and late-night socializing.
Prices range from ₩55,000-70,000 per night.

items.n: Fairfield by Marriott Busan Songdo Beach
items.d: The price is about ₩180,000 per night.
The cost is around ₩65,000 per night.
The cost is ₩30,000-40,000 per night.
The cost is ₩30,000-35,000 per night.

A modern and well-equipped hotel, ideal for early morning departures or late-night arrivals at Gimhae Airport. Rooms are spacious and clean, offering good soundproofing. Offers shuttle service to airport.
A mid-range motel offering reliable, clean accommodation near a major transit hub. Good for travelers prioritizing convenience and budget over luxury.

Offers spectacular views of Busan Harbor and the city lights. A stylish hotel offering one of the best panoramic city views from its rooftop cafe. While it is just outside Busan/West, its proximity to the old town and scenic views make it a
A clean and practical hotel for visitors looking to stay near the quieter Dadaepo Beach. Excellent base for watching the Dadaepo Sunset Fountain of Dreams and exploring Molundae.
A budget-friendly motel in the Gupo area, known for offering very clean rooms at affordable rates. A good no-frills option for short stays.
Offers modern amenities and themed rooms close to Busan's famous cultural village. Provides a comfortable retreat after exploring the village's steep hills.
A newer, high-quality hotel option in the Sasang area, offering spacious 'suite' style rooms. Provides a comfortable base near the Seobu Bus Terminal.
A clean, affordable motel within a short walk of Dadaepo Beach. A good option for budget travelers wanting a seaside location.
A standard, reliable motel choice in the Sasang area. Offers basic comforts and easy access to transportation and local restaurants.
A well-maintained hotel near Gupo, offering modern room facilities and private bathrooms. Suitable for both short layovers and longer stays.
A comfortable and stylish motel often chosen by business travelers due to its proximity to the bus terminal. Rooms are modern and relatively spacious.
Offers excellent views of Songdo Beach and the surrounding cable car system. A great mid-range option for those who want to wake up to the sound of the ocean.
A practical and budget-friendly motel for visitors to Dadaepo. It is close to the Metro Station and the beachside promenade.
Offers renovated rooms and comfortable bedding. It is a quiet option despite being close to the busy Gupo transit area.

A reliable, internationally recognized budget brand offering clean and functional rooms. While in Haeundae, it serves as a good affordable option for those willing to take the subway to Busan/West sights.
A comfortable hotel offering good access to the city's commercial and tourist heart, making it an alternative base for exploring the western side of Busan.
A clean and affordable motel known for its helpful staff and basic but well-maintained rooms. Ideal for budget travelers using the Sasang transport hub.
Specifically designed for travelers flying in or out of Gimhae Airport. The hotel is modern, providing excellent service and a comfortable stay for short layovers.
A rare guesthouse option in the western part of Busan. Popular with solo and budget travelers, offering dorms and private rooms with a relaxed, beachfront atmosphere.
A simple, budget-conscious motel near the beach. It provides a straightforward sleeping option, often with a view of the surrounding hills.
